text: Conservatism: Ger. Conservatismus ; Fr. conservatisme ; Ital. conservatismo . (1) The strong love of what is old, customary, and familiar, in opinion, social life and organization, religion, morals, &c. (2) In sociology: habitual opposition to change in social institutions, usages, or manners. 'We scruple not to express the belief that a truer spirit of conservatism, as to everything good in the principles and professed objects of our old institutions, lives in many who are determined enemies of those institutions in their present state, than in most of those who are themselves conservatives' (J.S. Mill, Dissertations and Discussions , i. 202). See LIBERALISM. Literature : see under SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY, and SOCIOLOGY. ( F.H.G. , J.M.B. )
